title: Quantum Gates
raw_text:
Quantum Computing Lessons - Mid-Way Structured
Edition (Lessons 6-10)
Lesson 6: Quantum Gates
Quantum Concept: Quantum gates are unitary operations that rotate, flip, or shift qubit states. They
preserve information while transforming amplitudes and phases. Basic gates like X, H, and Z enable
control over quantum behaviour. Gates operate reversibly, giving quantum circuits their unique
structure.
Analogy: Trading actions: buy, sell, hedge, or rebalance. These actions shift the state of a stock in
predictable ways. Just as gates rotate or flip a qubit, trading decisions rotate the market position.
Combined Insight: Quantum gates act like precise trading moves-each action changes future
trajectories while preserving underlying structure.

title: Single-Qubit Rotations
raw_text:
Lesson 7: Single-Qubit Rotations
Quantum Concept: Rotation gates (Rx, Ry, Rz) adjust a qubit's position on the Bloch sphere. They
allow fine-grained control of amplitude and phase. These rotations generalize basic gates into
continuous transformations.
Analogy: Dance movements: changing hand direction, posture, or rhythm in classical Indian dance.
Small adjustments shift the entire expression and outcome.
Combined Insight: Rotations in quantum space resemble nuanced dance transitions-precise,
continuous adjustments that shape final form.

title: Bloch Sphere
raw_text:
Lesson 8: Bloch Sphere
Quantum Concept: The Bloch sphere visualizes any single-qubit state as a point on a sphere. It
reveals amplitude balance, phase, and direction. It is a powerful tool for understanding rotations and
gate effects.
Analogy: Steering wheel or flight joystick: tilting in different directions controls movement. Small angles
create big trajectory changes.
Combined Insight: Like steering a vehicle, positioning a qubit on the Bloch sphere determines its
future evolution.

title: Multi-Qubit Systems
raw_text:
Lesson 9: Multi-Qubit Systems
Quantum Concept: Multiple qubits combine into larger Hilbert spaces via tensor products. The state
space grows exponentially. Multi-qubit systems can encode correlations and complex interactions.
Analogy: Family with multiple children-each child has unique traits but belongs to one shared
environment. The family's dynamics expand with each member.
Combined Insight: As families grow, dynamics become richer; similarly multi-qubit systems grow
exponentially in complexity.

title: Tensor Products
raw_text:
Lesson 10: Tensor Products
Quantum Concept: Tensor products combine qubits into joint states, creating basis states like |00>,
|01>, etc. They define composite systems and interactions. Quantum circuits rely on tensor structure to
process many qubits together.
Analogy: Two families merging through marriage-each combination of siblings creates new relational
configurations. Possibilities multiply rapidly.
Combined Insight: Tensor products expand possibilities like merged families creating a wider
relational landscape.
